intro.help: This intro is a short film that plays as you scroll or swipe, and stops when you stop. Each line stays until it has been read. Space plays the next line, Shift and Space goes back, W or the down arrow drives on and S or the up arrow backs up, and Escape skips the intro. The full script follows as text.

hero.sceneLabel: Sunset drive over a causeway toward a neon city skyline and an art-deco tower at the end of the avenue, palm trees on both sides
hero.speaker: Jesús
lines: I'm from Tenerife, where even the sun works overtime.
I'm a frontend engineer, and I solve problems for a living,
especially the ones that turn up on a Friday afternoon.
Before code, I did four years in the army as a combat engineer,
on Gran Canaria, which takes some nerve if you're from Tenerife.
I learned to take orders there, and now I give them to AI.

suspects.description: A police line-up of Jesús's four cats in front of a height chart, each behind a numbered plate. Tom and Kira stand the tallest, Odin a little lower, and Dante, the kitten, is the smallest by a head.

tips.text: This film is not suitable for passengers: nothing moves until you scroll or swipe, because you're the one driving.
Hold right-click over the scene, or hold Q, and the radio wheel opens. Let go over a station to tune in.
Press and hold the picture, or tap the radio button, and the radio wheel opens. Then tap a station to tune in.
Space brings up the next line, W or the down arrow drives on, S or the up arrow backs up, and Esc skips to the end.
Swipe up to drive on and down to back up. A tap on the picture brings up the next line, and Skip cuts to the end.
He follows F1, so every subtitle has a pit-lane limiter: the car waits until you've read it, however hard you push.
BABYLON's disco comes as standard, but the dial also has CROCKETT's eighties synth and K-CALIMA's classic rock.
MR. WOLF solves problems with hard rock, LEAVE THE GUN brings the funk, and LOVE DADDY spins nineties hip-hop beats.
The car never actually moves. The whole city drives past it, and so far nobody has had the heart to tell the car.
After the drive, his four cats face a line-up over scratched wardrobes and chewed cables, though only one did it.
Later on, a stats screen measures his appetite. The bar runs out long before he does.
Between The Godfather, Pulp Fiction and The Sopranos, he has watched enough crime to know a good getaway car.
At night the city lights a sign for every employer he has had, which is more neon than any CV has ever deserved.
Metal Gear taught him that a cardboard box is a fine place to hide. A loading screen isn't, so this one won't last long.

stats.title: PAUSED
stats.description: This is a pause screen. Its map is Tenerife, more or less, with the towns renamed: it traces his career as five main missions, four completed and one still running, and hides his favourite games, films and series, and his Formula 1, as places on the island. Beside the map, his saved games; the second tab is his character sheet, with his skills and records.

projects.title: Side projects
projects.speaker: Jesús
projects.line: I made these side projects on my own time, on nobody's dime.

dotfiles.title: DOTFILES
dotfiles.oneLiner: My whole machine as code: CachyOS and Hyprland, one composition per machine, simulated before it lands, rolled back if it fails.

tessera-studio.title: TESSERA STUDIO
tessera-studio.sub: Zero dependencies, because it works alone.
tessera-studio.oneLiner: A local, read-only browser for Tessera catalogues, with their reusable components, inventory and reuse decisions, written in Python with zero dependencies and a strict CSP.

project-atlas.title: PROJECT ATLAS
project-atlas.sub: An evidence sidecar for coding agents.
project-atlas.oneLiner: An evidence sidecar for coding agents: it maps a frontend project (components, design evidence, decisions, risks) before the agent changes code.

expenses-log-app.title: EXPENSES LOG
expenses-log-app.sub: A reminder before every charge, even offline.
expenses-log-app.oneLiner: A mobile-first PWA for recurring expenses, built with Next 16: smart lists, one tap to mark a bill paid, Web Push reminders before each charge, offline use and Supabase sync.
